To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the apparent mean DP of fructan increases in the order wheat, tall fesuce, timothy; that the concentration of low DP (<10) and high (>/=10) fructan is similar in leaf blades of wheat and tall fescue but is very low in leaf blades of timothy; and that the concentration of high DP fructans is similar in leaf elongation zones of wheat and tallfescue but is higher in leaf elongation zone of timothy.
the mean degree of polymerisation of fructan was highest in timothy, and that wheat and tall fescue had both low and high degree of polymerisation fructan, but timothy did not.
fructan in leaf blades of tall fescues and timothy is a high DP fructosyl fructose polymer, but that wheat has a low DP fructosyll transferase product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
fructan composition in mature leaf blade and the elongation zones of three grass species.
fructan in leaf tissue and not the more abundant starch in leaf blades.
the nature and DP distribution of fructan and the distribution of fructans between the elongation zone and mature leaf blade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fructan in all species is composed of a series of fructosyl-fructose units linked via a 2-1 beta-linkage.
wheat and tall fescue have high DP fractans, whereas timothy has low DP fructans.
wheat, tall fesue, and timoty have high DP frutcan in the leaf blades, and that wheat has low DP fructans in addition to high DP fructans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fructans from the three species differ in mean DP, and that fructan from wheat is composed primarily of 1-kestotetraose.
the nature of fructan and its apparent DP is species dependent and that the elongation zone contains higher DP fructan than the mature leaf blade.

the fructan in leaf blades of wheat is predominantly inulin with a small amount of 1-kestotriose, that in tall fescue is predominantly neokestose with a large amount of 1,1-kestopentaose and inulin, and in timothy it is predominantly inulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fructans in the three species are structurally different, but the nature of the fructans in wheat, tall fesuce, and timothy was similar to that found in other graminaceous plants.
the mean fructan chain length in the leaf blade of tall fescues and timothy was greater than that in wheat.
the fructan in timothy is a mixture of high DP fructans and fructans of lower DP, while the other two species contain high DP fructoligosaccharides in addition to high DP fructo-oligosaccharide.
